prerequisites: Basic knowledge in business administration and management (organization, innovation and marketing, finance and controlling, as well as production and logistics).
Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Entrance and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: apply the knowledge, tools and instruments required for performance management throughout the employee lifecycle.
evaluate analytical and synthetic skills for assessing complex socio-economic problems and critically discussing alternative or conflicting theories and concepts.
identify gender-relevant and gender-sensitive aspects of human resource management and leadership.
explain the theoretical foundations and basic tools of human resource management and leadership.
present an introduction and theoretical foundations.
describe the organization of human resource management.
plan human resource planning, recruitment and selection.
conduct performance and compensation management, training and further education.
explain leadership and management principles.
analyze HR controlling and specific topics of human resource management.
Critical thinking
Argumentation skills
Ability to cooperate
Conflict resolution skills
Gender competence
organize teamwork, conflict management and cooperative tasks.
discuss experience-based case studies, role plays and homework.
present insights and results from experience-based learning activities.
evaluate alternative approaches and conflicting concepts in role plays and case studies.
analyze personal and team performance in experiential learning activities.
summarize insights from interactive elements and exercises.
discuss applied theories and concepts from a meta-perspective.
represent evidence-based positions during meta-level theory discussions.

syllabus_topics: HR planning, recruitment and selection, including relevant gender aspects
Performance and compensation management, training and development, including relevant gender aspects
Leadership and management, including relevant gender aspects
Specific topics of human resource management, especially the use of AI
teaching_methods: Interactive course elements based on experiential learning techniques such as case studies, role plays, teamwork, and homework
Discussion of applied theories and concepts
